scene: A stick-figure caveman in a fur tunic stands at left with one finger on his chin and eyes drifting sideways toward a snarling lion lying on a grey stone slab. A raw steak sits in front of the lion and a cut-away red meat wedge shows in its flank, with three green wavy stink lines rising above its back and two small ones above the steak. A campfire, a thatched hut and acacia trees fill the savanna behind.
mechanism: Sets up a visual paradox: a campfire and raw meat are both present, yet the figure hesitates, so the viewer wonders what stops him from eating the lion. The question is carried by the pose and the stink lines rather than by extra words.
composition: Two focal points on a left-right split: the caveman at left third and the lion's head near the right-centre, linked by his sideways glance. The yellow headline spans the full top band; the grey slab acts as a stage that separates the lion from the ground. Small clutter (hut, campfire, trees) sits in the periphery.
typography: Three words in yellow with a thick black outline across the top, sized to roughly a sixth of frame height. The text is the largest element and survives at 160x90. It does not name the animal or species, so the title carries 'predator meat' and 'humans'.
colors: Saturated sky blue over ochre-yellow ground with an orange lion and a bright yellow headline; the red steak is the only strong red accent. The yellow text pops against blue but the lion's orange body blends into the ochre ground.
psychology: The caveman's round eyes glancing sideways, small flat mouth and finger-on-chin pose signal thinking, while the lion's bared teeth and angled angry brow add menace. Together they imply a puzzling danger rather than urgent fear.
partnership: Title asks why humans cannot eat predator meat; the thumbnail asks 'why not eat?' beside a lion and a steak, so it mostly restates the question with a visual scenario. It adds the stink lines as a hint of the answer without giving it away.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the lion's snarling face, then the caveman's hesitant stance, finally the steak and campfire.
art: Flat vector cartoon with uniform outlines and flat fills; the figure and lion share one line weight. The scene is cleanly layered and readable on a phone, though the thin stick limbs and tiny campfire lose detail at 160px.
strength: Clear one-line question with a funny contradictory image (a lion on a plate beside a steak) that reads in under a second.
weakness: The lion's orange fur merges with the ochre ground and the headline is generic, so nothing names what is being avoided.
bottleneck: Missing subject specificity: viewers cannot tell if the issue is flavour, disease, or danger.
action: Hypothesis: add a small red 'X' or parasite icon over the lion's flank cut-out to test whether a disease cue raises specificity over the plain steak.
counterexample: Seq 12 uses the same yellow-on-blue 'WHY ...EAT?' formula but makes the lion's dominance over a dead bear the single image, which is more dramatic and less cluttered.
hero_object: lion on stone slab with steak
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A grinning grey-bearded cartoon retiree in a bucket hat, red polka-dot neckerchief and blue polo winks while riding a small folding bicycle. Strapped to the rear rack are a fishing rod, a folding camp chair and a paper bag of oranges, and an open cardboard box labelled STUFF sits at bottom left.
mechanism: Reframes retirement as owning less: a cheerful rider on a folding bike with a few belongings (rod, chair, bag of oranges) next to a box labelled STUFF. Analyst reading: 'LIGHTER' can be read as carrying less baggage; no wealth cue is visible.
composition: The cyclist is centred left and the headline occupies the right 45% on pure white, so the picture and the words split the frame cleanly. The diagonal of the bike and fishing rod leads the eye up-left; the box labelled STUFF anchors the bottom-left corner. There is a lot of white negative space.
typography: Two words in huge condensed sans, 'RETIRE' in black and 'LIGHTER' in red, stacked right with generous letter size. It survives easily at 160x90. The title's 'Less is More' idea is echoed rather than extended.
colors: White background, black headline, one red word, and a restrained palette of blue, forest green and brown on the rider. The red of LIGHTER matches the neckerchief, tying text to figure.
psychology: The wink, broad smile and relaxed pedalling convey contentment and playful confidence; there is no fear or urgency cue. The elderly character signals the target viewer's own life stage.
partnership: Title 'Why Less is More in Retirement' and the thumbnail 'Retire Lighter' make the same promise, so the picture adds the lifestyle visual (fishing, groceries, bike) the title lacks. Little curiosity gap remains.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red LIGHTER and black RETIRE first, then the winking face, then the loaded bike rack, finally the STUFF box.
art: Clean digital vector-style cartoon with soft shading and consistent outlines; the bicycle wheels and spokes are drawn carefully. No visible compositing error, and the figure holds up at mobile size.
strength: Instantly readable lifestyle metaphor with strong text-image balance and a single red accent word.
weakness: The image is whimsical but the money angle (savings, spending) is not visible, so finance viewers get no number or stake.
bottleneck: Low tension: a happy cyclist makes a pleasant rather than urgent promise.
action: Hypothesis: replace the STUFF box with a small price tag or '$' symbol to test whether a money cue raises relevance without losing the lightness theme.
counterexample: Seq 14 does the opposite: a shocked large face with a billion-scale number creates alarm where Seq 2 offers calm reassurance.
hero_object: folding bicycle loaded with gear
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with swept dark hair and a deep scowl lounges in a red armchair with a laptop on his lap and white-socked feet up, a lilac polo on. At right a small round wooden table holds two tall stacks of gold coins with green starburst glows, and a thick black curved arrow points down to them.
mechanism: A lazy-looking figure beside two glowing coin stacks suggests wealth builds while you are passive; the age marker '40S' names the audience and the arrow marks the payoff object.
composition: The armchair figure fills the left half; heavy two-line headline fills the upper right; the coin stacks at lower right are the arrowed secondary focal point. The arrow runs from the text toward the coins, creating a clear Z-path.
typography: Five words in black extra-bold condensed caps in two lines, large enough to read at 160x90. 'MOVES' is a vague verb, and the title's phrase 'milestones' is not reflected in the image.
colors: White background, black text, red chair and gold coins as warm accents, with a pale green burst behind the coins to signal value. The lilac shirt and grey laptop are low-saturation.
psychology: The furrowed brows, wide round open eyes and downturned mouth read as a scowl, grumpy or suspicious rather than relaxed, which conflicts with the effortless-wealth idea in the headline and arm-chair pose.
partnership: Title 'Major MONEY Milestones To Accomplish in Your 40s!' and thumbnail 'Wealth Moves in Your 40s' share the age frame; the thumbnail adds coin stacks but not any actual milestone, so the title carries the list-like promise.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the 'WEALTH MOVES' headline, then the scowling face, then the black arrow to the coin stacks.
art: Digital cartoon with clean outlines; the foot and laptop overlap are plausible. The arrow and starburst are flat overlays but no lighting inconsistency is visible, and the arm-chair figure remains legible at small size.
strength: Clear hierarchy of bold headline, character, and arrowed coins, with the age marker inside the headline.
weakness: The scowl contradicts the 'easy wealth' message and the coin stacks are small relative to the figure.
bottleneck: Emotion and message mismatch weakens the hope cue.
action: Hypothesis: swap the scowl for a smug or relieved expression and enlarge the coin stacks to test whether emotion-message alignment lifts clarity.
counterexample: Seq 19 reuses the same layout with a smug half-lidded face, which fits 'passive wealth' better than Seq 3's scowl.
hero_object: two gold coin stacks on side table
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: [Q] / Would it be possible to get your teeth to such a cold temperature that they would shatter upon drinking a hot cup of coffee? / — Shelby
scene: Vertical artwork (about 404px wide) centred on blurred grey side bars: a pale grey question card with a circled Q badge, then a wavy thought bubble containing a thermometer with a red bulb and a row of outlined teeth, and below it a black-outline stick figure at a computer desk holding a mug.
mechanism: The reader-question format is itself the hook: an absurd physical what-if posed in plain text. The sketch gives a two-object preview (thermometer, teeth) but no answer.
composition: Top-to-bottom stack: question card, thought bubble, desk figure. The centred column leaves wide empty blurred bars, so the usable artwork is only about a third of the frame width. The thought bubble is the main visual focus with the card above it.
typography: 25 words of small serif text in a card, regular weight and black on light grey, far too small to read at 160x90; the card is an unreadable grey box and the bold byline is not distinguishable. The text does not duplicate the title and carries the whole question.
colors: Near monochrome: white page, black line art, mid-grey blurred bars and a single red thermometer bulb as the only accent. Contrast is fine inside the card but low overall impact.
psychology: The line-drawn figure sipping coffee is neutral; no face detail, no fear or authority cues.
partnership: Title 'Weird and worrying questions' is a generic label; the thumbnail supplies a concrete weird question, so it adds content, though the worrying element is not visible.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: grey question card first, then the red thermometer and teeth in the bubble, then the stick figure at the desk.
art: Hand-drawn minimalist line art on an off-white card with typical Shorts blurred-bar padding. The thin lines and small type collapse at 160px and the grey bars dominate the thumbnail area.
strength: Intriguing physical what-if with a recognisable single-icon preview (thermometer plus teeth).
weakness: Tiny question text and thin strokes are unreadable on mobile, and the blurred bars waste most of the frame.
bottleneck: Mobile legibility: the question, which is the hook, vanishes at 160x90.
action: Hypothesis: crop to the thought-bubble only and set 'TEETH vs COFFEE?' in large type to test whether the hook survives at phone size.
counterexample: Seq 18 puts one huge word and one large character in the whole frame; Seq 4 spreads thin detail across a narrow column.
hero_object: thermometer and outlined teeth in thought bubble
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: URINARY / TRACT / INFECTIONS / IN AGING / [Leslie Kernisan, MD MPH] / [Chrissy Kistler, MD MASc]
scene: Two rounded video-call tiles at right show a smiling dark-curly-haired woman in a black top against a white wall and a laughing woman with wavy light hair in a mustard sweater, each with a printed name-and-credential label. A small round line-art logo sits top-left and the headline fills the left side.
mechanism: Credibility-first packaging: named clinicians with printed MD credentials beside a plain topic label. It signals an expert conversation rather than a promise or a hook.
composition: The two tiles are stacked at the right with a shared left edge, roughly spanning the headline's height (tiles about y 85-628 vs headline about y 125-600), giving a stable but static layout.
typography: Five headline words on four lines in huge black sans, with the final line 'IN AGING' in white, plus two small caption labels. The headline is readable at 160x90; the caption names turn to smudges. The text repeats the title's topic but omits 'Symptoms & Prevention'.
colors: Dominant aqua-teal background with black and white type and neutral-toned tiles; no warm accent, so nothing competes but nothing pops either. Black on teal has strong contrast, white 'IN AGING' is somewhat weaker.
psychology: Both women are smiling or laughing, which is warm and approachable but gives no concern signal for an infection topic. The visible MD credentials supply the authority cue.
partnership: Title 'UTIs in Older Adults: Symptoms & Prevention' is echoed by the headline on topic only ('UTIs' spelled out, 'Older Adults' becomes 'IN AGING'); 'Symptoms & Prevention' is absent, so the image adds only the identity and credentials of two speakers and no symptom or prevention detail.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black 'URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS' first, then the upper webcam face, then the lower laughing tile, and last the 'IN AGING' line.
art: Screen-capture style tiles composited onto a flat colour in a template layout; webcam images are lower-resolution than the type. Clean edges, no obvious defects, but little depth.
strength: Clear topic statement and visible clinical credentials add trust for a health audience.
weakness: Full duplicate of the title with no reason-to-click, and the laughing expressions clash slightly with an infection subject.
bottleneck: No curiosity gap: the topic is stated but no symptom, number or question is posed.
action: Hypothesis: add one concrete hook phrase such as 'CONFUSION? NOT ALWAYS A UTI' (if supported by the content) to test whether a specific claim outperforms the bare topic label.
counterexample: Seq 14 uses a dramatic large face and number, whereas Seq 5 delivers a calm topic label with credentials.
hero_object: two webcam interview tiles
medical_notes: Neutral topic label with printed MD credentials and no cure, diagnosis or fear claim; the video content was not read.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man in a white tee and jeans stares open-mouthed at a calculator held in both hands. A cracked pink piggy bank with chipped pieces on the floor and a bundle of green banknotes lie at lower right; a black curved arrow points from the headline to the cash and piggy bank.
mechanism: A paradox in the headline (being poor costs more) is dramatised by a shocked man, a cracked piggy bank and an unexpected cash stack. The dollar sign in the final word makes the cost motif visible inside the text.
composition: Character on the left third, a big two-line headline on the upper right, and the piggy-bank-and-cash cluster at the bottom right as the arrow target. The three-part Z reading path is clear and generous white space isolates each element.
typography: Four words in black condensed ultra-bold caps, the 'S' of EXPENSIVE replaced by a dollar sign, taking about a third of frame height. Legible at 160x90. The title adds the 'why' and the 'pay more for everything' detail the thumbnail omits.
colors: White ground with black text, pink pig, vivid green cash and a skin-tone face; the green cash is the sole saturated accent and sits at the arrow tip. Good subject separation.
psychology: The wide eyes, dropped jaw and calculator stare signal dismay and a financial shock; the cracked pig adds vulnerability. It works as a recognisable worry cue for a money-stress audience.
partnership: The title 'The Math of Being Broke (Why You Pay More for Everything)' and the headline 'BEING BROKE IS EXPEN$IVE' make the same claim; the calculator visual echoes 'math' and the cracked piggy bank adds a scarcity image. The 'why' and 'pay more for everything' detail remain only in the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: 'BEING BROKE' headline, then the shocked face, then the arrow into the piggy bank and cash.
art: Family-sitcom-style cartoon with clean outlines and flat colour; the calculator buttons and pig crack show detail. Slight mismatch: cash stack is a fresh bundle despite the 'broke' story. Reads well at mobile size.
strength: Strong text-image fit: calculator plus cracked piggy bank illustrate the headline literally and the arrow guides the eye.
weakness: The fresh stack of cash next to the broke pig muddles the story, and the shocked face is a common template.
bottleneck: A mixed signal: money is present in a thumbnail about being broke.
action: Hypothesis: replace the banknote bundle with a receipt or fee tag to test whether the 'costs more' idea reads more clearly than a cash pile.
counterexample: Seq 10 shows a pile of glowing cash with a thoughtful face, so it signals abundance where Seq 6 signals scarcity.
hero_object: cracked piggy bank and calculator
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: At viewer-left a raw ham-on-bone with a pile of blueberries, raspberries and small orange fruit in front; at viewer-right a heap of roots, tubers, acorns and walnuts, with a blue dusk landscape visible through the cave mouth at upper right.
mechanism: A blunt question over a figure offered two choices of raw food: meat and berries versus roots and nuts. The 'before fire' premise is implied by the cave and the absence of any fire.
composition: The caveman is dead centre and faces the viewer; the two food piles flank him left and right, creating a symmetrical balance. The yellow headline occupies the whole top band and slightly overlaps the cave ceiling. The cave opening gives a bright secondary focus at upper right.
typography: Two yellow outlined caps words, 'ATE WHAT?', across the top at huge scale, very legible at 160x90. The text does not mention fire; the title supplies 'Before Fire'.
colors: Muted earth browns with olive-grey cave walls, bright yellow headline as the sole high-chroma element, plus small blue-berry and red-berry accents. The brown figure's fur blends into the cave floor but his white head stands out.
psychology: Round eyes glancing sideways and a small open mouth show puzzlement; the arms spread out with hands resting on the two food piles and the dim cave lighting give a slightly unsure mood rather than fear.
partnership: Title 'What Did Humans Eat Before Fire?' asks the question and the thumbnail reduces it to 'ATE WHAT?' plus the options, so the image adds visible candidate foods while remaining a close paraphrase.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow 'ATE WHAT?' first, then the large white face, then the left ham-and-berries and right roots-and-nuts piles.
art: Flat digital cartoon with a darker, slightly noisy cave background; the legs of the stick figure are cropped at the bottom edge. The food items are small and lose detail at 160px; background is moderately busy.
strength: Direct high-contrast headline paired with a symmetrical choice of two food piles invites a guess.
weakness: Dark brown cave background and small foods make the answer options hard to parse at phone size.
bottleneck: The key objects (the foods) are too small and low-contrast to carry the question.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the ham and the tubers to roughly twice their size and lighten the cave floor to test whether the food choice is read at 160px.
counterexample: Seq 1 shows the same caveman style in a bright blue-sky scene, so its foreground reads more clearly than Seq 7's dark cave.
hero_object: meat and berries versus roots and nuts
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: About twenty tiny white-robed figures stand or walk on the paved plaza, mostly in a cluster left of the column.
mechanism: Scale and specificity: the whole span of Roman history is packaged as one date range over a monument skyline, promising completeness rather than a puzzle.
composition: Colosseum anchors the left; the sky gap at upper right holds the serif headline and date line, forming a clean text window. The monuments are layered by depth, with the column providing a vertical accent near centre. No arrow or person leads the eye.
typography: 'ROME' in a large black serif with a smaller '753 BC – 476 AD' beneath, both at upper right on empty sky. The serif is legible at 160x90 but the date line is thin. The title's 'ENTIRE History' and '12 Minutes' hooks are absent.
colors: Warm sandstone and terracotta against pale sky blue; low saturation overall with a restrained palette. The black serif on light blue has good contrast, but no single accent colour.
psychology: No face or gesture; the cues are historical authority and epic scale, with a calm documentary mood and no urgency or emotion.
partnership: Title 'The ENTIRE History of ROME in 12 Minutes' promises compression and speed; the thumbnail only shows the place and dates, so it supports 'history' but leaves out the time-challenge hook.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: Colosseum mass first, then 'ROME' in the sky, then the date line, and last the plaza detail.
art: Detailed illustrated cityscape with an engraving-like outline and consistent warm lighting; building proportions are coherent. Very fine architectural detail becomes a dense texture at 160px but the main shapes still read.
strength: Instantly legible subject and time frame with a strong landmark that suits a history audience.
weakness: No prominent human or readable emotional element and no curiosity prompt, so it reads like a textbook cover; tiny plaza figures are visible.
bottleneck: Missing hook: nothing in the image signals why to click now.
action: Hypothesis: add a '12 MIN' stopwatch or ticking-clock graphic next to the date line to test whether the speed promise lifts the title partnership.
counterexample: Seq 9 puts the viewer in a vivid human scene with tension, whereas Seq 8 shows only a landscape of monuments.
hero_object: Colosseum
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A first-person view across a candle-lit dinner table in a Japanese-style room: two arms covered in dragon and peony tattoos reach forward, one hand presenting an open ring box with a sparkling diamond. Across the table a dark-haired woman in a black halter dress laughs and raises a champagne flute, while two black-suited silhouettes stand in the shoji doorways at left and right under paper lanterns, with a Mount Fuji scroll behind her.
mechanism: POV role-play: the viewer's own tattooed arms offer a ring, while faceless suited guards in the doorways signal danger. It combines romance with menace to evoke the 'wife of a yakuza boss' premise without any words.
composition: The ring box at right of centre and the woman's laughing face at the upper centre form the two focal points. The tattooed forearms enter from both lower corners as a frame, and the symmetrical guard silhouettes bracket the scene. Strong depth with table perspective leading to the woman.
typography: No text. The title carries the entire premise ('Your Life as the Wife of a Yakuza Boss'), so the image relies entirely on iconography (tattoos, guards, ring) to be understood.
colors: Warm amber lantern light and cream tablecloth against dark brown wood; the black suits create flat dark shapes and the diamond is the brightest point. Tattoo blue-grey adds a cool accent against skin tones.
psychology: The woman's open laugh and raised glass suggest delight and luxury, while the featureless guards add an ominous undertone. The mix of romance and threat produces intrigue rather than overt fear.
partnership: The thumbnail visualises the title directly: a ring proposal, tattoos for the yakuza link and bodyguards. It adds the romantic-yet-risky tone, and since there is no text the title must supply the identity.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the sparkling ring box first, then the laughing woman's face, then the tattooed arms, last the two black silhouettes.
art: Comic-style illustration with strong inked outlines and warm lighting; perspective on the table is consistent. Fine details (tattoo scales, cutlery) are dense, and at 160px the ring and woman remain readable while the guards become dark blobs.
strength: Rich story in one frame: proposal, danger, and wealth are all visible without text.
weakness: Dense scene detail and zero text make the narrative harder to decode at small sizes.
bottleneck: No short text anchor to focus the viewer on the premise.
action: Hypothesis: add a two-word label such as 'YAKUZA WIFE' in a high-contrast block to test whether a text anchor strengthens recognition at 160px.
counterexample: Seq 8 uses a comparable illustrated-scene approach but shows only monuments and tiny figures with no human action, so Seq 9's POV proposal-and-guards story is the stronger story proposition.
hero_object: diamond ring box held in tattooed hand
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man in a white shirt with rolled sleeves stands at left with a hand on his chin and eyes looking up and aside. Beside him a messy pile of banded green banknote bundles glows with a green aura, and two red question marks float above it; a thick black arrow at lower right curls towards the cash.
mechanism: A concrete number ('$2,000/MO') answers the title's 'extra cash' with a visible stack, while the red question marks and chin-touch pose raise the 'what now?' question.
composition: Man on the left edge, cash pile centre-left, headline top-right, arrow bottom-right: a diagonal flow from text down to money. The red question marks add small secondary focal accents. Good negative space on the right-bottom quadrant.
typography: Two lines in black ultra-bold caps: 'EXTRA' on top and '$2,000/MO' below, which is wider but about the same cap height, with '/MO' set smaller; two words total.
colors: White background with black text, a vivid green glow around the cash and bright red question marks; a blue-jeans and white-shirt figure stays neutral. The neon-green halo creates a strong subject separation.
psychology: The thoughtful, slightly uncertain look and floating question marks signal indecision, not distress; the glowing money adds a hope or temptation cue.
partnership: Title 'POV: You Paid Off Your House... Now What? (How to Handle the Extra Cash)' is condensed into a monthly dollar figure, adding a specific amount the title lacks and mirroring the 'now what' with the question marks.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: '$2,000/MO' first, then the glowing cash pile, then the thinking face, and finally the red question marks.
art: Same cartoon family-guy style as other Nick Invests thumbnails, with clean outlines; the cash pile is rendered with slightly more detail and a glow that reads as an overlay. The black arrow is crisp. Reads well at 160px.
strength: The concrete dollar amount plus a glowing cash pile gives a clear, quantified payoff.
weakness: '/MO' is small and the figure-with-money template is common, so the thumbnail does not suggest the 'house paid off' story.
bottleneck: Missing context: a house or mortgage cue is absent so the number lacks a story.
action: Hypothesis: add a small house icon with a 'PAID' stamp near the man to test whether the paid-off-home context increases relevance for the target viewer.
counterexample: Seq 6 shows scarcity (cracked piggy bank) where Seq 10 shows abundance (glowing cash), against the same cartoon template.
hero_object: glowing pile of banded cash

text: If you’ve been worried about / your aging parent / What to check next time you visit / & / How to talk to them about it / Leslie Kernisan, MD / BetterHealthWhileAging.net
scene: at right seven centred lines of text on white: two headline lines, three body lines ('What to check next time you visit' / '&' / 'How to talk to them about it'), then the name line and the URL.
mechanism: Credential-led slide: the topic is a relatable worry for adult children, with a named MD and a website. It promises practical advice, but the packaging resembles a title slide rather than a thumbnail.
composition: The black letterbox bars above and below squeeze the active slide to a wide strip of about 16:9 or wider, roughly 480x260 inside the 480x360 frame.
typography: About 26 words in small centred regular-weight sans-serif text at two sizes (headline slightly larger, body smaller).
colors: White slide background with black text, small blue-green accent on 'MD' and the URL, and a muted portrait; the black bars are the strongest dark element. No warm or alarm colour.
psychology: The woman's gentle smile, white coat and stethoscope present approachable medical authority; the opening words 'worried about your aging parent' name the viewer's concern but in small type.
partnership: Title '🆘 Does Your Parent NEED HELP? How to Talk to Aging Parents' is urgent in tone, while the thumbnail text is calm and descriptive; they overlap on the topic but the slide supplies the speaker identity and subtopics.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the portrait first, then the first line 'If you’ve been worried about', then the name and URL at the bottom.
art: Native image is only 480x360 with letterbox bars (letterbox cropped flag true), so it is soft and low-resolution; the portrait is a standard photo with no compositing. A plain slide with no depth, and it fails at small sizes.
strength: Visible MD credential and a human face establish trust for a sensitive family topic.
weakness: Small-type paragraph slide with black bars is unreadable on mobile and has no visual hook.
bottleneck: Mobile legibility: every line of text is too small to read at 160x90.
action: Hypothesis: crop the bars and set only 'WORRIED ABOUT YOUR PARENT?' in three large words beside the portrait to test whether the opener works at phone size.
counterexample: Seq 5 from the same channel keeps one huge headline and shows two named doctors, so its text survives at 160x90 where Seq 11's does not.
hero_object: portrait of woman in white coat with stethoscope
medical_notes: Slide presents a family-communication topic with a printed MD credential and no cure, diagnosis or fear claim; the content was not read.

scene: a dead brown bear lying flat on the ground with X-marked eyes and its tongue lolling out. Flat dark-green acacia trees at left and right and a tan savanna sit behind under a bright blue sky.
mechanism: A dramatic apex-predator image, one animal visibly killed by another, poses the question of why the winner will not eat the kill. The X eyes make the outcome unambiguous and darkly comic.
composition: The lion's roaring head is the primary focus at upper-centre-right with the bear's body as a diagonal base beneath it. The headline spans the top and the mane overlaps the letters 'ER', creating some collision. Acacia trees on the left and right edges frame the scene.
typography: Three yellow outlined caps words stretched edge to edge across the top, large and highly legible at 160x90. The text is vague about 'what' to eat; the title supplies 'predators eat each other'.
colors: Bright cyan sky, tan ground and orange-gold lion, with yellow type: high saturation overall. The brown bear separates well against the pale ground, though the headline yellow and the lion's golden fur are close in hue.
psychology: The open-mouthed roar and bared claws project aggression and dominance; the bear's X eyes and lolling tongue add shock and dark humour. It is a threat cue without a human subject.
partnership: is compressed to 'WHY NEVER EAT?', which drops 'predators' and 'each other'; the lion-over-bear scene supplies the missing subject and shows one predator killing another.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline, then the lion's open mouth, then the bear's X eyes, then the savanna trees.
art: Simple MS-Paint-like flat cartoon with thick black outlines and unshaded fills, slightly rough linework. The lion and bear read at 160px, and the mane overlap with lettering is a minor clutter issue.
strength: One clear, bold dramatic image whose lion-over-bear story reads instantly with a huge headline.
weakness: The mane overlaps the headline letters and the rough rendering looks less polished than other thumbnails in this batch.
bottleneck: Headline-art collision where the lion's mane crosses 'NEVER'.
action: Hypothesis: lower the lion by about 10% of frame height or shrink the headline slightly so the mane does not cross the letters, then compare legibility.
counterexample: Seq 1 uses the same formula but with a thinking human and a calmer scene, and so is less dramatic than Seq 12.

scene: A cartoon man with black hair and a white tee stands at left, shocked with an open mouth and eyes wide, lifting a giant green dome-lid off a green piggy bank full of green coin stacks. A few more coin stacks sit on the floor; a thick black curved arrow points from the headline to the pig.
mechanism: A named numeric rule ('10:1') plus a revealing action (lifting the lid of a coin-filled piggy bank) suggests a secret formula for saving. The ratio is stated but its meaning is withheld.
composition: Man at far left, piggy bank at lower centre, and the headline at upper right, joined by the arrow. The oversized green lid is the largest object and runs across the headline, creating overlap and a crowded centre.
typography: The headline sits in front of the green lid. The black '10:1' overlaps the lid's black underside and rim, so the first '1' loses its edge contrast and merges with the lid; the glyphs themselves are not cut off. Readable at 160x90, but the black-on-black overlap lowers legibility of the number.
colors: Monochrome green for the piggy bank, lid and coins on white, with black outlines and text; blue jeans on the man. The single-hue green gives strong brand-like consistency and good contrast with the white background.
psychology: Surprised, wide-eyed wonder suggests that he has discovered something valuable; hope and reward cues dominate and no fear is shown.
partnership: Title 'The Chinese Rule That Builds Wealth' and thumbnail 'The 10:1 Rule' share 'rule' and the thumbnail adds the specific ratio, but the cultural 'Chinese' element is not shown, so the pair complements each other.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: '10:1 RULE' first, then the green lid and piggy bank, then the shocked face, then the arrow.
art: Same sitcom-cartoon style with clean outlines; the lid clipping behind the headline looks like a layering mistake rather than an intended overlap. The green pig and coin stacks read clearly at small size.
strength: A memorable numeric hook with all-green imagery that ties the money theme together.
weakness: The lid overlaps and truncates the '1' in '10:1', and the ratio's meaning is undefined.
bottleneck: Text-art collision on the key number reduces its clarity.
action: Hypothesis: shrink the lid or move it left so it no longer covers the '1', then test whether the numeric hook reads more cleanly at 160px.
counterexample: Seq 10 keeps its number text fully clear of artwork, while Seq 13 lets the lid cut into the figure.

text: BY 2035? / 4 BILLION / PEOPLE / World Obesity Day
scene: Photoreal-style close-up of a man with wide eyes, open mouth and both hands pressed to his head, red and blue rim light on his face. A bathroom scale dial fills the bottom-left, and at upper right a small Earth globe shows glowing red fracture lines. Large orange-white lettering announces a population figure.
mechanism: Fear-scale shock: a panicked face, an oversized scale and a cracked Earth turn a statistic into a global-threat image. The year question adds a countdown.
composition: The face fills the left half as the primary focus, the number block sits at right-centre as the secondary focus, and the globe at upper right and scale at bottom frame the corners. The headline's '4' is oversized. Strong depth and vignette separate the subject from the dark background.
typography: Eight words in three sizes: small white 'BY 2035?', large gradient-yellow '4 BILLION', white 'PEOPLE', small 'World Obesity Day'. '4 BILLION PEOPLE' survives at 160x90 while the label lines turn small. The thumbnail's figure differs from the title's '8 Billion Reasons'.
colors: Near-black navy background with red and blue rim lights, a golden-yellow number gradient and white text. Very high contrast, warm accent on the number, and red cracks on the globe act as a warning cue.
psychology: Wide eyes, raised brows and open mouth plus hands on head signal shock and alarm; the scale and cracks reinforce a fear frame. Authority cues are limited to the 'World Obesity Day' label.
partnership: Title 'World Obesity Day 2026: 8 Billion Reasons to Act on the Obesity Pandemic | Obesity News' and the thumbnail share the event name; the thumbnail swaps the title's rhetorical '8 Billion' for a different figure and a 2035 projection, so the numbers need source checking.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the panicked face first, then '4 BILLION', then the cracked Earth, then the scale dial.
art: Photoreal dramatic composite with strong lighting; the scale dial numerals are out of sequence (0, 160, 120, 140 and a duplicate 140) which is a visible rendering inconsistency, and the red-fractured Earth is a stock-style graphic. Overall polished but with detectable artefacts.
strength: Highest emotional impact in the batch: large expressive face plus a huge number on a dark high-contrast background.
weakness: Fear-exaggerated imagery with an unsourced '4 BILLION' claim and a scale dial with garbled numerals undermine credibility.
bottleneck: Credibility: dramatic fear styling without a stated source or definition of the measured group.
action: Hypothesis: add a short qualifier such as 'OVERWEIGHT OR OBESE (PROJECTION)' under the number to test whether a clear scope line maintains attention while improving credibility.
counterexample: Seq 2 is calm and cartoonish with no number; Seq 14 is the opposite with a fear face and statistic.
hero_object: oversized bathroom scale and cracked Earth
medical_notes: A panicked face, cracked globe and an unsourced '4 BILLION PEOPLE BY 2035?' figure frame obesity as a global catastrophe, and the thumbnail figure differs from the title's '8 Billion Reasons'; the content was not read.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: NEED WORK / OIL / Great Depression / 1973 Oil Crisis / BANK / Global Financial Crisis / Covid-19 Pandemic
scene: A 2x2 grid of four hand-drawn boxed panels on white: a sad seated stick figure by a red brick wall beside a standing figure holding a NEED WORK sign on blue; a leaking OIL barrel on bright green; a cracked, crumbling BANK building on red; and a black biohazard symbol on yellow. Each has a cursive caption beneath.
mechanism: A list-of-events grid delivers the promise 'every crisis' as four distinct colour-coded panels, offering a quick completeness check rather than a puzzle.
composition: Perfect 2x2 symmetry with four equal panels and captions, centred on white with margins at left and right. No single focal point; each panel competes equally. Generous white space in the margins but no arrow or hierarchy.
typography: 14 words of cursive-script captions, medium size and thin strokes, plus tiny in-art labels (NEED WORK, OIL, BANK). At 160x90 the captions blur and only the colour blocks and the icons survive. There is no headline text; the title carries '10 Minutes'.
colors: Four saturated panel backgrounds (blue, green, red, yellow) with black line art; the vivid grid is eye-catching but the colours are arbitrary rather than semantic, except red for the bank collapse and yellow hazard for the pandemic.
psychology: The only faces are two tiny sad stick-figure faces (frowning, down-turned mouths) in the top-left panel; at phone size they vanish, so the emotion is carried by icons rather than a face.
partnership: Title 'Every Financial Crisis Explained in 10 Minutes' is illustrated by four named crises, which makes 'every' tangible, although it lacks the time-boxed promise and the word 'explained'.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow biohazard panel first for contrast, then the red bank collapse, then the blue worker panel and the green oil barrel, then the captions.
art: Hand-drawn doodle style with consistent thick outlines and radial gradient backgrounds. The icons are simple and recognisable, but the cursive captions and small in-art text fail at phone size.
strength: Colour-coded panels with iconic symbols let a viewer grasp 'multiple crises' at a glance.
weakness: No headline, small cursive captions and four equal panels leave no clear focal point.
bottleneck: Hierarchy: nothing tells the viewer which element to read first.
action: Hypothesis: add one large headline word such as 'EVERY CRISIS' across the top and enlarge a single panel to test whether a clear primary anchor lifts hierarchy.
counterexample: Seq 18 has one huge word and one big image, which Seq 15's four equal panels do not.
hero_object: four crisis panels (bank collapse, oil barrel, biohazard)
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with ginger hair and a grey tee presses both hands to his cheeks with wide eyes and a dropped jaw. At right a line chart with a red falling line is labelled JOB OPENINGS on the vertical axis and TIME on the horizontal axis, with seven small black worker silhouettes each crossed out by a red X, and a curved black arrow points to the line's downturn.
mechanism: A shocked reaction face plus a falling chart of crossed-out workers dramatises job-loss risk and the ellipsis suggests something unfolding right now.
composition: The reacting man fills the left third; the headline sits top-right and the chart below it with the arrow pointing down at the red trend line. A clear top-to-bottom flow from text to evidence. The chart and the figure are balanced but the chart is detailed.
typography: 'IT'S HAPPENING...' in black caps on two lines at very large size, plus tiny axis labels that vanish at 160x90. The headline is strong but vague; the title adds '2026' and 'lose your job'.
colors: White background, black headline, red falling line and red X marks as the warning accent, with a neutral grey shirt. The red-on-white chart gives high contrast for the warning colour.
psychology: Hands-on-cheeks horror, bulging eyes and open mouth communicate panic; the red X marks and falling line reinforce job-loss anxiety. It is a strong fear cue for a worker audience.
partnership: Title 'Why Everything Changes After You Lose Your Job In 2026' is about personal job loss; the thumbnail shares the job-loss theme but reframes it with a macro declining job-openings graph, and the headline 'IT'S HAPPENING...' adds urgency the title lacks (debatable escalation).
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: 'IT'S HAPPENING...' first, then the horrified face, then the red falling line and crossed-out workers.
art: Sitcom-style cartoon with clean lines; the chart is a flat overlay with silhouettes that are fairly detailed for the size. The headline and face survive at 160px but the axis labels and silhouettes do not.
strength: Immediate emotional narrative: a reaction face and a red downward trend make the threat obvious.
weakness: The chart's tiny labels and seven silhouettes add clutter that does not survive on mobile.
bottleneck: Chart detail that is invisible at small size dilutes an otherwise strong reaction image.
action: Hypothesis: reduce the chart to a single bold red falling arrow and delete the silhouettes and axis labels to test whether a simpler graphic raises mobile clarity.
counterexample: Seq 13 uses a wide-eyed discovery face with a money object, which is the hopeful opposite of Seq 16's panic.
hero_object: falling red job-openings chart with crossed-out workers

scene: A smirking grey-haired businessman in a navy pinstripe three-piece suit with a burgundy tie and white pocket square sits behind a dark wooden desk with both hands flat on a sheet of paper. A curved black arrow runs from the word YOU to his head; black letterbox bars sit above and below the white frame.
mechanism: The title's role-play ('you're the CEO who lost $613 billion') is reduced to an accusation aimed at a smug executive; the arrow turns the viewer into the person responsible.
composition: The figure is centred-left at large scale, with the three-line text stacked at right and the arrow linking text to the head. White space is generous. The symmetrical desk pose and crop give a stable but static composition.
typography: Three words in a hand-lettered black style with 'LOST' in red and larger; large enough to read at 160x90. The text omits the amount and company names, so the title carries '$613 Billion' and 'Lehman Brothers'.
colors: White background, navy suit and red accents on the tie and the word LOST; the red word is the only highlight. Strong figure-ground separation but a restrained palette.
psychology: A closed-mouth smile with a slightly lowered brow and direct gaze at the viewer, with no wide eyes, open mouth or visible tension; this reads as calm rather than distressed, which does not match the loss implied by 'LOST'. The formal three-piece suit signals wealth and authority.
partnership: Title 'POV: You're the Lehman Brothers CEO Who Lost $613 Billion' and thumbnail 'YOU LOST IT' make the same accusation, with the image adding a stereotyped executive. The dollar figure and firm name sit only in the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red 'LOST' first, then the smirking face along the arrow, then the suit and desk.
art: Polished semi-realistic digital illustration with tidy shading; the lower-resolution 480x360 source is upscaled and letterboxed with black bars. The hands on the desk look slightly stiff, and the figure remains legible at 160px.
strength: Direct second-person accusation with a single red word makes a bold, quick message.
weakness: The smirk contradicts the loss message and the figure is a generic stock-executive look with no reference to a crash.
bottleneck: Emotion and message mismatch: a smiling executive does not look like someone who lost $613 billion.
action: Hypothesis: change the expression to a stunned or ashen look and add a falling red stock line behind him to test whether the loss story becomes visible.
counterexample: Seq 16 pairs a panicked face with a falling chart for a similar loss theme and aligns its expression with its text; Seq 17 does not.
hero_object: pinstriped executive at wooden desk

scene: A sweating stick figure with a large round head, a blue sweat drop and a worried flat-mouth expression stands at left. At right a green dragon head with yellow eye and bared teeth breathes a large orange-and-yellow flame that stretches towards the figure.
mechanism: The one-word question over a dragon attack pairs a fantastical image with an obvious puzzle: why do creatures like this not exist? The tension of fire pointed at the figure draws attention.
composition: A strong right-to-left band of fire, running from the dragon's mouth and rising slightly towards the upper left, links the two characters, with moderate white space around the head and flame.
typography: A single word 'WHY?' in thick hand-drawn black letters about a fifth of the frame high, instantly readable at 160x90. The title supplies 'Don't Dragons Exist', so the single word relies on the picture.
colors: White background with a strongly saturated orange-yellow flame and a green dragon, black text and linework; the flame is the highest-energy accent and the sky blue sweat drop adds a small cool contrast.
psychology: The stick figure's side-eyes and sweat drop show nervous unease, while the snarling dragon is aggressive. It reads as playful peril rather than genuine fear.
partnership: Title 'Why Don't Dragons Exist?' is carried by the dragon and 'WHY?'; the image shows a dragon that appears to exist and be attacking, which adds a mild contradiction as it asks why it doesn't.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: 'WHY?' first, then the orange flame, then the dragon's eye and teeth, last the sweating stick figure.
art: Hand-drawn digital style with uneven fills; the dragon is shaded in more detail than the plain stick figure, giving a deliberate style clash. The dragon's head is cropped at the right edge, but the thumbnail stays simple and strong on mobile.
strength: Single huge word plus a vivid flame creates a minimal, high-contrast question that survives at tiny size.
weakness: The dragon is cropped and the detail style mismatch with the stick figure looks uneven.
bottleneck: Little title context: a lone 'WHY?' depends entirely on the video title.
action: Hypothesis: add a small 'DRAGONS' label or a crossed-out dragon silhouette to test whether naming the subject improves the question's clarity.
counterexample: Seq 15 has no dominant word and four equal panels, in contrast with Seq 18's single focal word.
hero_object: fire-breathing green dragon head

VALUE. / FRESH PRODUCE / GREAT PRICES EVERY DAY! / High & Steady Consumer Demand / Scalable Business Model / Multiple Revenue Streams / GROCERIES BEVERAGES BAKERY OTHER ITEMS / High Profit Potential / Prime Location High Foot Traffic / Efficient Operations Control Costs / Inventory Management Reduce Waste / Customer Retention Build Loyalty / LOYALTY CARD
scene: A photoreal-style supermarket entrance with a green FRESH MART sign sits in the centre inside a ragged torn-edge mask, surrounded by eight annotation callouts with small icons: a shopper group and cart, four category tiles, a map pin and a shop awning, boxes and a barcode scanner, a produce crate with a tablet and recycle symbol, a loyalty card and bag, a pie chart with coins and a rising bar chart with a coin.
mechanism: An infographic-style overview packs a business case into one frame: each callout names a reason owning a grocery store is attractive. It reads as a lesson overview rather than a single hook.
composition: Headline at top, store image centre, callouts arranged around it radially with curved arrows pointing inwards. Visually symmetrical but extremely dense; the store image is the main focus and eight icon-text pairs compete at the edges. The thin red underline under the headline marks the header.
typography: About 60 words in five sizes: huge black-and-green headline, then several small captions at sizes that blur at 160x90. The headline is readable; the callouts are not. The headline repeats the title's subject and adds nothing numeric.
colors: White background, black and forest-green headline, mostly green store signage with multi-colour icons (red, yellow, blue pie chart, orange). Many accent colours spread evenly, which prevents any single focal accent.
psychology: The picture is neutral and corporate with no human face; the promotional tone ('GREAT PRICES EVERY DAY!') signals opportunity but conveys no tension or emotion.
partnership: Title 'The Economics of Owning a Grocery Store' and the thumbnail 'So You Want To Own A Grocery Store' share the subject; the thumbnail adds eight benefit callouts but it reveals the 'pros' list and none of the economic surprise.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: green 'GROCERY STORE' headline first, then the central FRESH MART storefront, and the surrounding callouts only after a pause.
art: Mixed-style collage: a photographic storefront with a rough torn mask, flat clip-art icons, and handwritten-style captions. The scale of the store sign and the generic invented brand 'Fresh Mart' make it feel like a stock template, and the icons are tiny at 160px.
strength: The headline and storefront image make the topic unambiguous and the infographic layout signals depth of content.
weakness: Roughly 60 words and about twenty small icons overload the frame; the callouts are unreadable on mobile.
bottleneck: Density: the callout layer competes with the headline and fails at 160x90.
action: Hypothesis: keep the headline and storefront and remove all eight callouts, then test whether a single margin figure such as '2% PROFIT' lifts curiosity.
counterexample: Seq 18 has one word and one image; Seq 20 has sixty words and sixteen icons.

scene: A vertical black line splits the frame. Left on pink: a sweating brown ape-like character with a strained face runs on a treadmill and a big red X is drawn across it. Right on pale green: a muscular, calm brown ape walks upright on a thinner treadmill with a green check mark curling across its body.
mechanism: A wrong-versus-right split (not a true before/after): strained running is crossed out while calm walking gets a tick. It communicates a better method visually in one glance, without text.
composition: Two equal panels split down the middle by a thick line; each ape is centred in its panel and the red X and green check mark create diagonal sweeps that cross both bodies. The strong left-right symmetry makes the comparison immediate.
typography: No text. The title ('Fastest Way To Get To 10% Bodyfat Explained By Ape') supplies the target and the ape brand; the image offers only the comparison and no number.
colors: Pink versus mint green backgrounds with a red X and a green check, brown apes and grey treadmills: a semantic red-wrong, green-right scheme with strong separation between panels.
psychology: The left ape's grimace and sweat drops show strain and struggle; the right ape's small smile and relaxed muscular stance show ease and confidence. It sets up aspiration through contrast.
partnership: Title promises the 'fastest way to 10% bodyfat'; the thumbnail suggests that walking beats hard running, which the title does not state; this is an implied claim that the content would need to confirm.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red X on the left ape first, then the green check on the right, then the contrasting faces, then the treadmills.
art: Rough hand-drawn cartoon with marker-style strokes and flat colour; the check mark and X are scribbled over the figures. Both panels are readable at 160px and the colour split carries the message.
strength: Instantly decodable do-this-not-that comparison using semantic colours and no words.
weakness: The thumbnail makes an implicit effectiveness claim (walking beats running) with no numbers, and the rough sketch looks low-production.
bottleneck: No text anchor to state the target outcome of 10% body fat.
action: Hypothesis: add a short '10%' badge on the right panel to test whether the outcome number is picked up at 160px and anchors the comparison.
counterexample: Seq 15 uses four panels with captions and no clear contrast, whereas Seq 21 uses two panels with one clear contrast.
hero_object: two apes on treadmills with X and check mark
medical_notes: The image implies that gentle walking is superior to hard running for reaching 10% body fat without stating any evidence; the video content was not read.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

A bearded man in glasses and navy scrubs sits at a desk with a keyboard, papers and white flowers, gesturing with raised hands. mechanism: A talking-doctor video frame with a burned-in caption about fatigue at rest, plus a pasted-in standing man as a symptom stand-in. The title's 'normal symptom' hook is not visible in the frame.
composition: Seated doctor in the upper centre with the standing man overlapping his lower-right side; the caption bar runs across the standing man's chest below the doctor's hands. The standing man is the largest element (about 57% of frame height) but both faces are tiny, all inside a ~404px column, and the grey bars occupy about 68% of the width, leaving little visual impact.
typography: Eight words in a small sans caption with a lime-yellow highlight, very small at 160x90. It reads as a mid-sentence subtitle ('This leads to...') with no antecedent, so it lacks a stand-alone hook. The title carries 'This 1 Normal Symptom Means Your Heart Is Failing'.
colors: Pale lavender-grey office wall, navy scrubs, grey t-shirt and blurred grey bars, with a glossy red-brown desk and burgundy chair as the warmest areas; the lime-yellow caption is the brightest element. Low saturation and low contrast overall.
psychology: The seated man's serious expression and hand gesture give a lecturing, authoritative impression; the pasted-in man looks neutral rather than fatigued, so the symptom is not shown emotionally.
partnership: Title 'This 1 Normal Symptom Means Your Heart Is Failing #heartdisease #danger #shorts' makes a strong fear claim; the thumbnail shows a mid-sentence caption about persistent fatigue at rest, the same topic, but it does not back the title's urgency.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow caption first, then the bearded man's face, then the pasted-in standing man.
art: Photographic video still with a cut-out composite: the standing man's cutout edges, flat lighting and scale relative to the desk do not match the office scene, which suggests a compositing artefact. Faces are tiny (about 1% of frame) and the image is dull at 160px.
strength: The presence of a scrubs-wearing speaker offers a basic expert cue.
weakness: The caption is a sentence fragment, faces are tiny and the pasted-in figure looks mismatched.
bottleneck: Mobile legibility and the narrow framing: the frame is mostly blurred bars with tiny elements.
action: Hypothesis: crop to the doctor's face with a large three-word overlay like 'HEART FAILURE? FATIGUE' to test whether a bold headline makes the symptom claim readable.
counterexample: Seq 14 has a huge face, a big number and strong contrast, whereas Seq 22 has tiny faces on grey.
hero_object: doctor in scrubs with composited standing man
medical_notes: A scrubs-clad speaker whose chest embroidery shows only a partly legible 'Dr.' prefix is paired with a healthy-looking pasted-in standing man and a fatigue caption under a title that says the symptom means heart failure; how the pasted figure relates to the speech was not checked because the content was not read.

His body is cropped at the legs along the lower left; headline text sits at right, with 'RETIREMENT?' on a bright yellow highlight bar running to the right edge.

colors: White background, black text, yellow highlight bar as the single accent and a grey suit with navy tie. The black-on-yellow bar is the strongest contrast in the frame.
psychology: The shrug, raised eyebrows and sideways glance convey puzzlement and mild scepticism; no fear or urgency is shown. The suit signals an advisor persona.
partnership: Title 'Who Has $1M in Retirement Savings? (Fewer Than You Think)' is mirrored by the thumbnail's question, and the shrug hints at 'fewer than you think' while the thumbnail leaves the answer unrevealed.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: '$1M' and the yellow 'RETIREMENT?' bar first, then the shrugging face, then the open palms.
art: Clean digital cartoon with a slightly stylised thin-line face; the figure is cut off at the legs and the text sits cleanly on white. Reads well at 160px, and the yellow bar is a crisp flat overlay.

weakness: The shrug is a stock pose and the thumbnail gives no visual of savings or a retiree.

scene: A grocery checkout scene: a figure in a navy cap and grey hoodie with a drawn smiling face (eyebrows, dot eyes) presses a finger to his lips in a shushing gesture and holds an open brown wallet at the counter; a phone with a teal glow and green chart sits on the counter beside coins. Beside him a woman in a green top who points, a man in a red jacket covering his mouth and a woman in a blue hoodie laugh; a smiling cashier in a blue uniform stands at left. Lane sign '6' and an EXPRESS sign appear in the background.
mechanism: A secret-keeping gesture over a payment moment: the shush and the glowing phone with coins echo 'never tell anyone', while laughing onlookers suggest the secret is being gossiped about.
composition: The shushing figure sits at the horizontal centre as the focal point; the three laughing bystanders form a cluster beside and to the right of him
typography: No overlay text; only incidental lane signs ('6', 'EXPRESS') in the scene. The title carries everything ('POV: Once You Get Money Never Tell Anyone These 7 Things'), including the number 7.
